sales_hooks: CXMT is the only Chinese HBM development program — its progress (or lack thereof) determines whether China's AI cluster buildout is HBM-constrained. SK Hynix/Samsung should track CXMT's technology node closely.

CXMT lacks EUV lithography (export-controlled) — this limits their HBM to DUV-achievable density, capping them at HBM2E/3 equivalent, 1-2 generations behind SK Hynix. This gap is a durable sales advantage.

China AI chip demand for HBM-equivalent is ~$2-3B/year and growing — if export controls limit Korean/US suppliers from selling to China, CXMT fills the gap. Monitor US export control decisions closely.
CXMT is state-backed with near-unlimited government funding — their trajectory is a policy risk, not a technology risk. Track MIIT funding announcements as leading indicators.

competitive_position.vs_sk_hynix: 2+ generation gap; no EUV access limits density and yield; not commercially competitive outside China
competitive_position.vs_samsung: Similar technology gap; CXMT's advantage is zero export-control risk for Chinese customers
competitive_position.risk_to_incumbents: Medium-term risk in China market only; no near-term threat to global HBM market
